topic.name: Solving Logarithmic Equations With Logarithms on Both Sides

question.text: Given that $\log {(10-4x)} = \log{(10-3x)}$, what is the value of $x?$
question.explanation:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

\begin{align*} \log {(10-4x)} &= \log{(10-3x)} \\[3pt] 10-4x &= 10-3x \\[3pt] x & = 0. \end{align*}

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation:

  • Substituting $x=0$ back into the original equation, we get \begin{align*} \log {(10-4(0))}&\stackrel{?}{=}\log{(10-3(0))}\\[5pt] \log(10)&=\log (10)\quad{\color{green}{\checkmark}} \end{align*} Therefore, $x=0$ is a valid solution.

example.title: Solving Logarithmic Equations Containing Linear Arguments on Both Sides

question.explanation:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

\begin{align*} \ln (3x+1) & =\ln (x-5)\\[3pt] 3x+1 &= x-5\\[3pt] 2x &= -6\\[3pt] x &= -3. \end{align*}

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation:

  • Substituting $x=-3$ back into the original equation, we get \begin{align*} \ln (3x+1)&\stackrel{?}{=}\ln (x-5)\\[5pt] \ln (3(-3)+1)&\stackrel{?}{=}\ln (-3-5)\\[5pt] \ln (-8)&\stackrel{?}{=}\ln (-8)\\[5pt] \end{align*} However, $\ln (-8)$ is not a real number.

Therefore, we conclude that the equation has no real solutions.

example.title: Solving Logarithmic Equations Containing Linear Arguments on Both Sides

question.explanation:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

\begin{align*} \log_8 \left(x^2+19x\right) & =\log_8 (10x-8) \\[3pt] x^2+19x & = 10x-8\\[3pt] x^2+9x+8 &= 0\\[3pt] (x+1)(x+8)&=0\\[3pt] x&=-1, -8. \end{align*}

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation:

  • Substituting $x=-1$ back into the original equation, we get \begin{align*} \log_8 \left(x^2+19x\right)&\stackrel{?}{=}\log_8 (10x-8)\\[5pt] \log_8 \left((-1)^2+19(-1)\right)&\stackrel{?}{=}\log_8 (10(-1)-8)\\[5pt] \log_8 \left(-18\right)&\stackrel{?}{=}\log_8 (-18)\quad{\color{red}{\times}} \end{align*} which is not valid because $\log_8 \left(-18\right)$ is undefined. Therefore, $x=-1$ is not a valid solution.

  • Substituting $x=-8$ back into the original equation, we get \begin{align*} \log_8 \left(x^2+19x\right)&\stackrel{?}{=}\log_8 (10x-8)\\[5pt] \log_8 \left((-8)^2+19(-8)\right)&\stackrel{?}{=}\log_8 (10(-8)-8)\\[5pt] \log_8 \left(-88\right)&\stackrel{?}{=}\log_8 (-88)\quad{\color{red}{\times}} \end{align*} which is not valid because $\log_8 \left(-88\right)$ is undefined. Therefore, $x=-8$ is not a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "No solutions."
